listing.name: Snowboard Kids (SnowboardKids-Recomp)
listing.summary: A native Snowboard Kids port for Windows and Linux. Select your own USA cartridge dump on first Play.

steps.title: Select your own supported original on Play
steps.instruction: Choose Play, then select your own Snowboard Kids (USA) ROM, game code NSKE, in the player's file chooser. Upstream ROM-IDENTITY.md specifies its normalized identity and the supported N64 byte orders. The player remembers where your ROM is, so keep the original where you selected it.

steps.title: Keep the complete package for your system
steps.instruction: For a copy you manage yourself, keep the whole package together: SnowboardKidsEngine.exe on Windows or SnowboardKidsEngine on Linux, the matching modules/snowboardkids-us game module, assets and runtime libraries. The published beta includes a precompiled module, so normal players compile nothing. To add that copy to Portcove, select the engine and its folder.

warnings: The package includes a modified RecompFrontend fork by cdlewis that the project license does not cover. Portcove downloads it only from the project’s own releases. You need your own original game files. Source and first-party checks do not confirm gameplay, real saves or installed behavior.
This is an upstream beta. Portcove has not observed native setup, gameplay or saves. A game module left in the profile's modules folder overrides the packaged one.

references.title: Preserve the actual profile and active module
references.instruction: Back up the player's profile before changing versions: normally %APPDATA%\SnowboardKids on Windows or ~/.local/share/SnowboardKids on Linux, unless SBK_USER_DATA_DIR selects another folder in a copy you manage yourself. It holds settings, the remembered ROM location, Controller Pak .mpk saves, .sbks save states, logs and any user game modules. Loading a save state does not rewind Controller Pak storage. A game module in that folder, or one named by --module or SBK_GAME_MODULE, takes priority over the packaged module, so remove an old one after updating. Close the player before replacing a copy you manage yourself.

presentation.manual_preparation: On first Play, select your own Snowboard Kids (USA) ROM, game code NSKE, in the player's file chooser; the player remembers its location and may keep its own copy in the profile, so keep the original where you selected it. Settings, Controller Pak saves, save states, logs and any user game modules go to the player's profile: %APPDATA%\SnowboardKids on Windows, or $XDG_DATA_HOME/SnowboardKids, usually ~/.local/share/SnowboardKids, on Linux. Portcove neither backs up nor removes the profile, and rollback does not rewind it; back it up before changing versions. A game module in the profile's modules folder takes precedence over the packaged one, so remove an old one after an update. Portcove replaces the player; you own the original and the profile. If no compatible game module loads, the player can run its bundled Python module builder; Portcove starts it without writing Python bytecode into the managed copy.
